facts.text: A scenario description language is a formal written format describing a test situation so a computer can generate and run it; a domain-specific language (DSL) is a small programming language built for one subject area.
facts.quote: A scenario description language is a formal written format for describing a test situation (who is where, moving how, under what conditions) so that a computer can generate and run it, and a domain-specific language (DSL) is a small programming language built for one subject area.

facts.text: A scenario language specifies positions, speeds, triggers and parameter ranges in simulator-readable form, including for a machine reversing toward a worker emerging from behind a stockpile in dust.
facts.quote: Where a catalog says "machine reverses toward a worker emerging from behind a stockpile in dust", a scenario language fixes positions, speeds, triggers and parameter ranges in a form a simulator can read.

facts.text: ASAM stands for the Association for Standardization of Automation and Measuring Systems.
facts.quote: ASAM is the Association for Standardization of Automation and Measuring Systems

facts.text: ASAM OpenSCENARIO XML version 1.4.0 (2026) describes precise, synchronized maneuvers for road vehicles tied to road networks; the booklet rates its off-road fit poor to moderate.
facts.quote: ASAM OpenSCENARIO XML (version 1.4.0, 2026; ASAM is the Association for Standardization of Automation and Measuring Systems) describes precise, synchronized maneuvers for road vehicles tied to road networks; its off-road fit is rated poor to moderate.

facts.text: ASAM OpenSCENARIO DSL version 2.2.0 (March 2026) makes abstract and logical scenarios, parameter variation and key performance indicators first-class concepts, which suits scenario families.
facts.quote: ASAM OpenSCENARIO DSL (version 2.2.0, March 2026) makes abstract and logical scenarios, parameter variation and key performance indicators first-class concepts, which suits scenario families

facts.text: ASAM OpenSCENARIO DSL has an on-road domain model and limited tool support; the booklet rates its off-road fit moderate.
facts.quote: but its domain model is on-road and tool support is limited; the fit is moderate.

facts.text: ASAM's off-road work identified missing scenario-description concepts for deformable terrain, airborne particles, vegetation, heavy-machine manipulation and sensor degradation.
facts.quote: ASAM's own off-road work identified missing concepts for deformable terrain, airborne particles, vegetation, heavy-machine manipulation and sensor degradation.

facts.text: Scenic 3 (peer-reviewed, 2023) is an open-source probabilistic language with native 3D geometry, occlusion-aware visibility and placement without lanes.
facts.quote: Scenic 3 (peer-reviewed, 2023) is an open-source probabilistic language with native 3D geometry, occlusion-aware visibility and placement without lanes

facts.text: The booklet rates Scenic 3's off-road fit good, but Scenic 3 is not an ISO or ASAM standard.
facts.quote: its fit is rated good, but it is not an ISO or ASAM standard [Chapter 9].

facts.text: The booklet recommends encoding the scenario catalog in a manufacturer-owned, domain-neutral, version-controlled form using either Scenic or an in-house YAML schema with an OpenODD-style taxonomy, and exporting to OpenSCENARIO for tools that require it.
facts.quote: encode the catalog in a domain-neutral, version-controlled form, either Scenic or an in-house YAML schema with an OpenODD-style taxonomy, owned by the manufacturer, and to export to OpenSCENARIO for tools that need it.

facts.text: No off-road scenario standard was found in development that could arrive before mid-2027.
facts.quote: No off-road scenario standard was found in development that could arrive before mid-2027 [Chapter 9].

facts.text: The choice of scenario description language determines whether thousands of concrete tests can be generated, varied and traced automatically.
facts.quote: The language determines whether thousands of concrete tests can be generated, varied and traced automatically.

facts.text: A road-oriented scenario description language would force every pit, bench and stockpile into an unsuitable lane-based model.
facts.quote: One built for roads would force every pit, bench and stockpile into a lane-based model that does not fit [Chapter 9].
